## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Amos 1:1-3:15 is read strictly verse-by-verse per the three-phase method: Phase 1 (above) isolates each verse's own inner-being phenomena in isolation, before any operation or cross-verse pattern is drafted. "Bearing on the inner being" is taken to include: (i) the LORD himself throughout — his own settled judicial resolve, his past benefactions recalled, his elective "knowing" of Israel, his own necessitating word; (ii) each nation as a corporate collective (Q8), its own crime and, where the text states it directly (Edom, 1:11; Ammon, 1:13), its own disposition; (iii) Israel specifically, both as a corrupted collective (2:6-8) and as the LORD's own uniquely accountable elect (3:1-2); (iv) named human roles (Amos, 1:1/3:8; the prophets/Nazirites, 2:11-12; unnamed office-holders throughout); (v) non-human entities whose state is described in direct relation to human life (the pastures/Carmel, 1:2; the fire and the unnamed adversary as the LORD's own instruments; the lion/bird/snare analogies of 3:4-5, set aside per step 2 note (d) where no human relation is stated within the verse itself). Per the phase-separation discipline (Part B.12), genuine literary/structural observations (the eight-oracle formula, ring-composition candidates, shared vocabulary across verses) are NOT treated as phenomena or built into operations — they are logged only in the emergent-questions log below.

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for all three chapters (184/184, 163/163, 165/165 non-particle spans). Per governance.verse_gap_by_design, three verses in this range have no row in iba.db (Amos 2:10, 2:13, 3:3) and are noted inline at each occurrence, not treated as errors.

**Corpus-continuity check.** No prior filled debate found for this book at or before this range — this is the first debate in the sequence (or nothing precedes it yet). Nothing to re-read.

## Phenomena register (Phase 1 output)

### Amo 1:1

> The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

**Phenomena identified (Phase 1).**
- Amos — his own added act of "seeing" the word, alongside its bare reception ("was"). Warrant: "which he saw" (H2372, chazah), distinct from a bare-reception opening. **Stated.**
- Uzziah, Jeroboam, Joash (named kings/father) — no phenomenon found, silent: named only as chronological anchors; no operation or state is attributed to any of them (step 3 note a).

### Amo 1:2

> And he said: “The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the top of Carmel withers.”

**Phenomena identified (Phase 1).**
- The LORD — an active, self-originating roar/utterance, going forth from himself (Zion/Jerusalem). Warrant: "roars... utters his voice" (H7580/H5414M). **Stated.**
- The pastures of the shepherds (non-human, in scope per note (b)/(d): its stricken state is described in direct relation to human shepherd livelihood) — a stricken, mourning condition, responsive to the LORD's roar. Warrant: "mourn" (H0056). **Stated.**
- The top of Carmel (non-human, in scope similarly, standing for the land's own fruitfulness) — a withering condition. Warrant: "withers" (H3001). **Stated.**

**Phenomena identified (Phase 1).**
- The LORD — a fixed, irrevocable judicial resolve — an interior stance of settled, unappeasable determination. Warrant: "I will not revoke [turn back] the punishment" (H7725O/H3808). **Stated.**
- Damascus (national collective) — a violent, unrestrained disposition, evidenced by a war-atrocity against Gilead. Warrant: "threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron" (H1758) — the act itself is stated; the disposition it evidences is **inferred**.

Warrant: the shepherd/lion simile, "so shall the people of Israel... be rescued, with the corner of a couch and part of a bed" (H5337). **Stated**, via the simile's own explicit application ("so shall...").
- "The people of Israel who dwell in Samaria" — the ironic object/recipient of this near-total "rescue"; own interior not stated (silence), only their reduced remainder.

**Phenomena identified (Phase 1).**

- Israel — the addressed party, its transgressions the stated ground of the judgment; own further interior not restated here (already established at 2:6-8/3:10) (silence this verse beyond being named).

### Amo 3:15

- Israel (propertied/ruling class, implied by luxury-house ownership) — the addressed party whose accumulated wealth is the object of judgment; own further interior not restated here (silence this verse).
